::: {#exm-racket-dfs}
#### Depth-first search in Racket

In Racket, `dfs` (@def-dfs) can return the list of marked vertices, in the order in which they were marked.
Two functions call each other:
`dfs-from` marks `v` and goes through its neighbors,
and `dfs-each` goes through a list `vs` of vertices,
calling `dfs-from` on each one that is not marked yet.
It uses `neighbors` from @exm-racket-neighbors.

```racket
(define (dfs-from G v marked)
  (dfs-each G (neighbors G v) (append marked (list v))))

(define (dfs-each G vs marked)
  (if (empty? vs)
      marked
      (if (member (first vs) marked)
          (dfs-each G (rest vs) marked)
          (dfs-each G (rest vs) (dfs-from G (first vs) marked)))))

(define (dfs G s)
  (dfs-from G s empty))
```

With the graph $T$ of @fig-triangles stored as

```racket
(define triangles
  '((1 2 3)
    (2 1 3)
    (3 1 2 4 5)
    (4 3 5)
    (5 3 4 6 7)
    (6 5 7)
    (7 5 6)))
```

`(dfs triangles 3)` returns `'(3 1 2 4 5 6 7)`, the order of @exm-dfs-trace,
and `(dfs office 'a)` returns `'(a b c e d f)`, the order of @sol-follow-first.

:::
